clue.text: Demand for many tissues finds selective process unwelcoming

parts.note: streaming is the school practice of sorting pupils into ability groups
a cold reception is an unwelcoming one

explanation.surface: A complaint that some selection procedure is giving applicants a frosty reception.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaming is the British school term for dividing pupils by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy head cold with a running nose makes a person get through box after box of paper hankies.

clue.text: First-class student on trees races round backwards

indicators.note: the race letters go round, enclosing the student and the trees

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
A1 means first-class, written AI
L for learner, the student driver's plate
firs are conifers

explanation.surface: A top student among the trees runs laps the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races; 'round' puts them around AILFIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in rear end leading is moving in reverse, so the phrase is an idiom for travelling the wrong way about.

clue.text: English river — English river with gravelly deposit

parts.note: the Esk is a river in Cumbria and Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A geographer notes one English river after another, each leaving gravel behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use the word for a long winding ridge of glacial gravel and sand, laid down by meltwater.

clue.text: See 10
Want walker with 9 body to have Prussian weapon

parts.note: to want is to need
a leg is what one walks with
9 is INTERNATIONAL, and the UN is an international body

explanation.surface: A hiker needing an international organisation to own a German army rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 9 means 'international', so an international body is the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dreyse rifle, fired by a long needle striking the cartridge, was the breech-loader of the nineteenth-century Prussian army.

clue.text: Detective on wheels has instrument for cheat

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
DS is Detective Sergeant
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A policeman in a car carrying a harp, which somehow makes him a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler at the card table is a cheat who wins by sleight of hand.

clue.text: Moor safely with some booty almost raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters run upwards, bottom to top
only part of the words is taken, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: Pirates tie up their ship safely, with nearly all the loot hoisted aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes OTYAL from booTY ALmost, and 'raised' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing usage, to bring a vessel to a stop and keep her stationary into the wind is to heave to.

clue.text: A lot of fish, a lot of spread, to say nothing prim and old-fashioned

parts.note: a school is a large group of fish swimming together

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: Marmite is a yeast extract spread on toast
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A list of breakfast items followed by a demand for silence, describing a stuffy old teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops TE from MARMITE to leave MARMI. Marmite is a British yeast-extract spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a strict old-time female teacher means being prudish, fussy and behind the times.

clue.text: Confine, at island, Lenin's first Communist organisation

parts.note: to intern is to confine, as in wartime
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Lenin's is taken

explanation.surface: Lenin's first revolutionary group, its members locked up on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comintern, the Third International, was the worldwide federation of Communist parties founded in Moscow.

clue.text: Insect seeking mate between 2 11s

parts.note: a cricket is a chirping insect
a match is a partner or equal

explanation.surface: A chirping insect looking for a partner between two others.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a cricket team, so a contest between two elevens is a game of cricket, England's bat-and-ball sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of the bat-and-ball sport is played by two teams of eleven players each.

clue.text: One of 14 that is appearing soon

parts.note: 14 is LORDS, and an earl is one of the peers
yon is the old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: A peer who is about to appear shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: At an early stage means shortly after the start, close in sense to soon.

clue.text: Present of iron from Paris

parts.note: fer is French for iron

explanation.surface: A gift made of iron sent over from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out for acceptance, a synonym of proffer.

clue.text: St Peter, etymologically, to scrub the deck

parts.note: St stands for saint, a holy person
the name Peter comes from Greek petros, rock or stone

explanation.surface: An etymological note on the name of Saint Peter, oddly linked to ship cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint gives the holy part; Peter's name means 'rock' in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors scoured wooden decks with a soft sandstone block, and the verb names that scrubbing.

clue.text: House of 9 10 4

definitions.meaning: the upper chamber of the UK Parliament is the House of Peers

explanation.surface: A venue where international cricket is played.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a famous London cricket ground; the other sense completes 'House of', the upper chamber of Britain's Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The British upper chamber is named after its peers, and the cricket ground is named after Thomas Lord.

clue.text: Don't talk about entering footwear for native Americans

indicators.note: the silence call and the word for about go into the footwear

parts.note: shoes are footwear
sh is a command to be quiet
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A request not to discuss stepping into shoes, which somehow describes a people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shoshone are an indigenous people of the western United States, plural here.

clue.text: Gets on bad with modifications for 9 10 4

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who gets on badly with changes at a sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is a Test cricket ground in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: The Birmingham ground is a venue that hosts Test cricket, so it is a place for such a match.

clue.text: Novel Gypsy damsel wandering outside period

indicators.note: the scrambled damsel letters surround the period
the letters of damsel wander into a new order

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A gypsy girl in a novel roams beyond her own time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns DAMSEL into ESMLDA, which goes outside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: The gypsy heroine of Victor Hugo's Notre-Dame de Paris is a girl of the Romani people in fiction.

clue.text: 9 pack to show if TVs are OK

definitions.text: to show if TVs are OK

parts.note: 9 is INTERNATIONAL, and a Test is an international cricket match
a pack is a set of playing cards

explanation.surface: A sports broadcaster checking that television sets work.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, England against Australia for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters once transmitted fixed images of patterns and colours so viewers could adjust and check their sets.

clue.text: Start of play on island with flexible toy

parts.note: Action! is the director's call to start filming
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Children begin a game on an island with a bendy toy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The poseable soldier figure with jointed limbs was a British boys' plaything.

clue.text: Assume there's an order to take a pew

parts.note: PO is a postal order, a money order bought at the post office
take a pew is a casual invitation to sit down

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is told to sit in a pew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is not a command here but a postal order.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit something is to put it forward as true for the sake of argument, to suppose it.

clue.text: Mesopotamian maybe disturbing Abraham's right

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: Something disturbs the right of the patriarch Abraham, himself from Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marsh Arabs live in the wetlands of southern Iraq, ancient Mesopotamia, so one is an example of a Mesopotamian.

clue.text: Come again about dog

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A stray dog keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that recurs happens again, repeatedly, coming back after an interval.

clue.text: Nearly illegitimate enough?

indicators.note: nearly all of the word is kept, its last letters dropped

parts.note: bastard means born out of wedlock

explanation.surface: Asking whether a child is almost illegitimate enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops RD from BASTARD. Basta is Italian for 'enough!', used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian exclamation for stop or that will do is borrowed into English with the same meaning.

clue.text: Look to circle on floor

parts.note: a deck is a floor on a ship, and to deck someone is to floor them
O is a circle shape

explanation.surface: Someone glances round a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Decko is British and Australian slang for a look, as in 'have a decko'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang borrowed from Hindi dekho, meaning look, used for taking a quick glance.

clue.text: Buy wildly into lawyer for president

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go into the lawyer's abbreviation

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

indicators.note: the letters move wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: A president who buys lawyers recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes UBY from BUY, which goes inside DA.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for George W. Bush mimics a Texan drawl of his middle initial, W.

clue.text: Security device keeps prisoner from drug

indicators.note: the seal holds the prisoner inside it

parts.note: a seal secures a container from tampering
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A security system keeps a prisoner away from narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconal is a brand of secobarbital, a barbiturate sleeping pill.

clue.text: Region of 9 qualification in type of opera

indicators.note: the qualification goes in the type of opera

parts.note: opera seria is serious opera
9 is INTERNATIONAL, and the IB is the International Baccalaureate

explanation.surface: A region known for its international qualification within a type of opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera seria is the formal, serious style of eighteenth-century opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast Russian territory east of the Urals is an area of northern Asia.

clue.text: Backing slave has always covered platform for the rejuvenated

indicators.note: backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a serf is a bonded labourer, a slave

indicators.note: the word for always covers the platform

parts.note: ay is an old word for always
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A slave stands on a platform, which perks up those who need a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' makes FRES from SERF; 'covered' puts DAIS inside AY.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile describes someone who has bounced back, lively and refreshed, much like those revived.
